compartment.title: Redesign Reading Archive UI
compartment.p1: I started by verifying the existing state for the Reading Archive component. I confirmed that the goal is a complete redesign of the archive experience, while adhering to several critical constraints: the page must remain mounted using `mountReact` and data attributes, not standard Inertia pages; existing Rails URL/filter behavior must be preserved; and no new packages should be introduced unless strictly necessary. The design mandates creating seven main sections: 1) HERO (with "RECOVERY LITERATURE" eyebrow); 2) BROWSE BY THEME (displaying available tags with Lucide icons and maintaining the "All" filter functionality); 3) READING GRID (must be responsive: 1 col on mobile, 2 on tablet, 3 on desktop); 4) READING CARD (with rounded corners, subtle shadow, strong title, readable excerpt, source/date metadata); 5) TAGS ON CARDS (tags must stay on ONE SINGLE LINE and use flex-nowrap; if overflow occurs, they should display "+N"); 6) TAG VISUAL IDENTITY (the first tag determines the card accent via a large, subtle Lucide icon background); and 7) SEARCH (must leverage existing Rails index endpoints for filtering). The implementation requires creating a migration to add `icon_name` to the `tags` model if it doesn't exist. For search functionality, I must ensure compatibility with both `params[:tag]` (for tag filtering) and add support for `params[:q]` (for searching title/content). Finally, I established strict testing requirements: verifying archive load, tag filtering, correct card rendering across breakpoints, and that clicking a reading still leads to the original `reading.path`.
compartment.p2: I designed the Reading Archive UI overhaul around several key functional blocks: HERO (displaying count stats), BROWSE BY THEME (filterable tags with Lucide icons), and READING GRID/READING CARD. The most constrained element is the TAGS ON CARDS, which must use `flex-nowrap` to keep all visible tags on a single line and display "+N" for overflow while retaining responsiveness. Crucially, I established that the page structure cannot deviate from its existing mount point (`mountReact`/data attributes). Furthermore, I defined the search flow: it needs to support both legacy tag filtering via `params[:tag]` and new full-text searching via `params[:q]`. The underlying technical dependency requires handling the potential missing `icon_name` on tags by running a migration, followed by data updates for all existing tags.
compartment.p3: The Reading Archive UI was redesigned into a modern component set comprising a thematic hero banner, a browsable tag filter, and a responsive reading card grid. The core architectural challenge resolved was enforcing the one-line constraint on display tags using CSS techniques like `flex-nowrap` while maintaining mobile responsiveness across 1, 2, and 3 columns at different breakpoints. This required establishing a new data pattern (via adding `icon_name` to tags) and ensuring that search functionality could gracefully handle both legacy tag filters (`params[:tag]`) and newly supported full-text query parameters (`params[:q]`), all while respecting the existing React/Rails mounting lifecycle.
compartment.p4: Reading Archive; mountReact; icon_name; lucide-react; flex-nowrap; params: tag, q

facts.PROJECT_RULES: * The Reading Archive must preserve existing Rails URL/filter behavior when displaying content. * Search functionality requires compatibility with both `params[:tag]` (for tag filtering) and optionally support for a query parameter `params[:q]`.
facts.ARCHITECTURE: * The Reading Archive component is mounted using `mountReact` and data attributes, not a standard Inertia page.
facts.CONFIG_VALUES: * Responsive reading grid columns: 1 (mobile), 2 (tablet), 3 (desktop). * Tag display constraint: Tags must remain on ONE SINGLE LINE across all breakpoints. * Migration required for tags: `icon_name` field added to the `tags` model.
facts.NAMING: * The component displaying tag icons should use a centralized Lucide icon mapping system rather than scattered JSX elements.

output.user_observations: * User provides extremely comprehensive, prescriptive instructions that cover design aesthetics (e.g., "Dark HumbleBot"), implementation details (e.g., specific React lifecycle hooks), and necessary data migrations across multiple layers of the stack.

primer_candidates.primer: How does the Reading Archive component ensure tag filters remain functional when migrating from a dedicated Rails controller/URL structure to an enhanced client-side mountReact setup?
